name: convexity-mcp

tools.name: get_component
tools.description: Get a component and all its attributes (values and storage types), looked up by name, INCLUDING which bus(es) it connects to (bus/bus0/bus1, by id and name where set). Use this to inspect a component before changing it — never guess a component's bus from its name.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: The projects the user can open and which project and model are open now. A project holds the user's models and the project's Files, shared with its members; a model is one energy system in it.

tools.name: open_in_app
tools.description: Open a model in the Convexity app (starting the app when nothing is running) and work on it from here on. Name it, with project when the name repeats across projects, or pass its id; list_projects lists them. When the name is in several projects and the user named none, ask which before opening either. path imports a .db file on this computer into the app's open project as a new model. create makes a new, empty model called name (ask the user for a name if none was given) in the project, with its time axis (naive UTC) and the default carriers, and opens it.

name.description: The model's name as the app shows it.

project.description: The project holding it (name or id). Default: the open project.

path.description: Absolute .db path on this computer: imported as a new model (with create and no app: where the new file goes).

create.description: A new, empty model called name.

tools.name: save_version
tools.description: Save the whole project as it stands (every model, file and dashboard) as a named version in Version History: before a large or risky change, or when the user asks for a checkpoint.

project.description: Project name or id; the open project when absent.

tools.name: restore_version
tools.description: Put the whole project back as a version held it (every model, file and dashboard; anything added since is removed, and a file goes to the Bin), only when the user asks to undo or go back; it always waits for their approval. version is an id or name from history (of "versions"). Edits not yet in a version are saved first, and the restore is itself a version, so it can be undone by restoring the one before. The restore runs on the server and takes up to a minute: this waits briefly, and if status is still "pending" read history (of "versions") until it says done or failed. Which version is meant must be clear: ask when it is not.

project.description: Project name or id; the open project when absent.

tools.name: search_docs
tools.description: Search the Convexity product documentation for how features work. Use when the user asks how to do something in Convexity or how a concept works.

tools.name: get_model_summary
tools.description: Overview of the open model: counts and capacity by type and carrier, scenarios, documents, values worth checking. aggregate:false lists each component with its bus and key inputs, for a review. For results, get_results. include adds: config (discount rate, solver, periods, currency), carriers.

tools.name: set_network_config
tools.description: Set one model-level parameter (e.g. discount_rate, unmet_load_active, or currency: the code the app labels money with, e.g. EUR) in the scenario named, as for any edit. How a scenario solves (solver, representative days, horizon) is run_settings.

param_value.description: The value, as a string (e.g. "0.05", "highs", "true"). Coerced to param_type by the backend.

scenario_id.description: Required: where the change goes. A what-if scenario by name or id (create_scenarios makes one), or "base" for the model itself, only when the user asked to change the model.

tools.name: run_settings
tools.description: How a scenario solves: solver, horizon (perfect foresight, representative days, rolling horizon) and solver options. Without set, reads the model's settings and each scenario's own. set changes one scenario (named, as for any edit; "base" is the model, only when the user asked), over the model's settings; reset true makes it follow the model's again. Nothing runs.

scenario_id.description: Required: where the change goes. A what-if scenario by name or id (create_scenarios makes one), or "base" for the model itself, only when the user asked to change the model.

horizon.description: perfect_foresight: one solve over every step; representative_days: builds on a few days per year, then dispatches every hour; rolling_horizon: windows with limited foresight; chunked_snapshots.

solver_options.description: The solver's own options; null removes one.

tools.name: list_validation_rules
tools.description: The attribute vocabulary. With no filter: an index — per component type, the attribute groups and attribute names (cheap; start here). Pass component_type for that type's rules (data type, unit, default, required, input vs result, timeseries allowed), optionally narrowed by group_name.

group_name.description: Only rules in this group (group names come from the index).

names_only.description: With component_type: return attribute names only.

tools.name: list_scenarios
tools.description: List all scenarios defined in the network, including their run status and descriptions. By default the 'Actual' scenario is excluded. Set include_actual=true when the user asks about actuals data or wants to compare actuals against other scenarios. Pass changes_for (a scenario id or name) for what that scenario changes: every input it sets, with the base value beside it; with against (another scenario), where the two differ instead.

include_actual.description: If true, include the 'Actual' scenario. Default is false.

changes_for.description: A scenario id or name: list what it changes instead.

tools.name: add_components
tools.description: Add components, many per call, of any type: BUS (with latitude and longitude), GENERATOR, LOAD, STORAGE_UNIT, STORE, LINK, LINE, TRANSFORMER. Buses in the same call come first, so a build can add buses and what connects to them together. A carrier the model lacks is created. scenario "base" builds into the model itself (every scenario sees it); a scenario adds them off in the base and on there (a what-if). Values are static inputs, e.g. {"p_nom": 100, "max_hours": 4}; fill series (p_set, p_max_pu) with set_series after. The reply lists each one made, inputs refused, and inputs left at a default that leaves it idle. Values taken from a project file: give source {path, sheet, row} (on the call, or per component) and each is cited to it.

scenario.description: "base" to build the model, or a what-if scenario.

source.description: The project file the values came from.
The project file the values came from.

tools.name: edit_components
tools.description: Rename components, move them to another bus (or a bus on the map), change their carrier, or delete them (delete: true; a bus with components on it also needs with_connected: true). Changes the model itself, for every scenario. Values go through set_values.

tools.name: edit_carriers
tools.description: Create, change or delete carriers: co2_emissions (tCO2 per MWh of fuel), max_growth (MW of new build allowed over the horizon; null for no limit), nice_name (display name), color. A carrier not in the model is created; delete: true removes one nothing uses. Carriers belong to the whole model, so every scenario sees the change.

tools.name: fill_weather
tools.description: Wind and solar capacity factor profiles (p_max_pu) at each generator's location from Renewables Vision, Convexity's own weather service (ERA5, 1940 to last year): to fill a model's profiles, or for weather sensitivities. One year goes in scenario ("base" for the model itself, else made if new); several years make an ensemble, one scenario per year named "<ensemble>/<year>". preview: compare years' average capacity factors without changing anything, e.g. to find the stillest year; for "how sensitive is it to the weather", preview, then offer an ensemble. Defaults to every wind and solar generator.

tech.description: Which generators, by carrier. Default both.

scenario.description: One year: the scenario to write into, by name or id, made if new; "base" only when the user asked to change the model itself.

preview.description: Only report each year’s average capacity factors.

tools.name: run_model
tools.description: Solve the open model as the Run button does: on this computer (local, free) or in the Convexity cloud (paid; only with the user's go-ahead, then pass confirm_cloud). Every run is recorded; its results become the current results of the scenarios it solved. Do not edit the model while it runs.

scenario_ids.description: Scenarios to solve, by id or name; "base" or null for the base network. Omit for the open scenario.

where.description: Default: the model's solver setting (always cloud on web).

confirm_cloud.description: Required true for a cloud run: the user agreed to pay.

representative_days.description: Capacity expansion on representative days (time-series aggregation) for this run: decide what to build on a few representative days of each year, then dispatch every hour with that fleet. Pass {} for the defaults.

foresight.description: myopic (default): year by year; perfect: all years at once.

wait.description: Block until the run ends and its results are in.

tools.name: runs
tools.description: The open model's runs, newest first: status, when, and which scenarios' current results each holds. Pass run_id for one run's status and error, and logs: true for the end of its solver log (cloud runs keep one; a local run does not).

tools.name: cancel_run
tools.description: Cancel a run of the open model: a cloud run, or a local run solving on this computer.

tools.name: show_in_app
tools.description: Switch the app to a page (overview is the Model page, results is Analytics, docs is the project's Files) or tab; table opens Tables on a component type, set up. To put one thing on screen use show_address.

tab.description: A tab of the Model page (implies page: overview).

table.description: Tables on one component type, set up. Columns by id or header.

filter.description: column → text, number, list of values, or {min, max}; {} clears

select.description: Select columns, down the named rows or all of them

tools.name: show_address
tools.description: Show the user something in the Convexity app by its address — the same token mentions use: a component on the map or in the grid ("[[component:generator/Tuas CCGT]]", "[[component:load/City|in=table]]"), a value in the grid or a series at a moment ("[[value:load/City|attr=p_set|at=2030-01-01T05:00]]"), a scenario ("[[scenario:High gas]]"), a dashboard ("[[dashboard:Results/Costs]]"), or several at once ("[[show:table|type=generator|names=A;B|cols=p_nom]]", "[[show:map|names=A;B]]"). Use it whenever the user should SEE what you are talking about.

address.description: The address token, with or without the surrounding [[ ]].

tools.name: ui_state
tools.description: What the user is looking at in the Convexity app: the page and tab, the active tab, the table type, the current model and scenario, and the components selected on the map. Cheap; call it before deciding what to show or when the user says "this".

tools.name: read_table
tools.description: The rows the Tables grid in the app shows, as tab-separated text: to check what the user sees, or that an edit reached the screen. With type it opens that table if it is not on screen; filter and sort set the table up on screen first, as show_in_app({table}) does.

filter.description: column → text, number, list of values, or {min, max}; {} clears

tools.name: read_skill
tools.description: Working notes for a kind of task (a health check, scenarios and sensitivities, analysing results), from the app's skills. Without name, lists them; read the one that covers a task before doing it the first time.

tools.name: set_user_expertise
tools.description: Record the user's experience of energy modelling (sets how much you explain) when they say it, or, once you can tell, with inferred: true.

tools.name: list_project_files
tools.description: The project's Files as JSON, a page at a time: its documents, data and code, shared by every model. prefix narrows to a folder ("docs/"); deleted lists the Bin.

tools.name: read_project_file
tools.description: Read a project file by path (or id): text, Markdown, CSV and code as lines; a spreadsheet as rows of one sheet; a PDF as text page by page, to cite. pages ("3", "2-5"), lines ("1-200") and sheet choose a part; the first by default. A CSV or sheet also gives each numeric column's mean, min and max over every row.

tools.name: search_project_files
tools.description: Search the project's Files for a phrase or words: text, Markdown, CSV, code and small PDFs on this device. Each hit has the file, page or line, and a ready [[source:…]] citation; read_project_file gives the context.

tools.name: write_project_file
tools.description: Write a text file to the project: a note, a CSV table, a write-up. A new path is created, folders included. from_results takes a get_results query and writes its whole table as CSV, uncapped. To change a file, pass expected: the sha256 read_project_file gave; if it changed since, the write is refused, so read it again. overwrite: true replaces it unread, only when told to. Never write keys: every member reads Files.

tools.name: organise_project_files
tools.description: Sort the project's Files, in order, stopping at the first failure: mkdir {path}; move {path, into} ("" = top level); rename {path, name}.

tools.name: get_sources
tools.description: Where the model's input values came from: each source cites a spot in a project file or a web page, for one value in one scenario. Narrow by component, type, attribute or file; scenario shows the sources backing what that scenario uses. Warnings say when the value or the file has changed since the source was added. unsourced: true instead lists the values set with no source, and how many are sourced by type.

scenario.description: Scenario name. Absent or "base": the base network, whose source also backs a scenario that keeps the base value.

tools.name: add_source
tools.description: Record where one input value came from, so anyone can check it. Only for a value you, or the user, took from that source. A project file is cited with the [[source:…]] token read_project_file or search_project_files gives: a quote must be the exact words in the file, and is refused otherwise. A web page needs its url and title. Each call is one value in one scenario; call it once per value.

scenario.description: Scenario name. Absent or "base": the base network, whose source also backs a scenario that keeps the base value.

cite.description: A project file: [[source:<path>|p=<page>|q=<exact words>]], |sheet=…|range=… for a spreadsheet, or just the path for the whole file.

accessed_on.description: When the page was read, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: today.

quote.description: The words on the web page that give the value.

note.description: How the value follows, e.g. "converted from $/kW".

tools.name: remove_source
tools.description: Remove a source by the id get_sources gives. Only with the user's word, or to replace one you added in error.

tools.name: list_comments
tools.description: The project's comment threads: who said what, and where (a table cell as type › component › attribute, or a file and its spot). Open threads by default. Narrow by file path or component name. Reply or resolve by a thread's id.

status.description: Which threads: open (default), resolved or all.

file.description: Only threads on this file path.

component.description: Only threads on this component, by name.

tools.name: add_comment
tools.description: Comment where people will see it, under the name Convexity: reply in a thread (reply_to: a comment's id from list_comments), or start one on a project file (file, with spot for a page, a sheet range, a row or a quoted passage) or on a value in the open model (component and attribute, and scenario when it is about one). Comment only when asked to, or to flag something a person should check.

reply_to.description: A comment id: the reply goes in its thread.

spot.description: Where in the file: {page} for a PDF, {sheet, range} for a spreadsheet ("C4:D6"), {row, column} for a CSV, {quote} for a passage of text.

scenario.description: Scenario name; absent or "base" for the base network.

tools.name: resolve_comment
tools.description: Resolve a comment thread once what it raised is done, or reopen it (resolved: false). Any comment id in the thread will do.

tools.name: sanity_check
tools.description: Run a read-only validation bundle against the current model DB. Returns { passed, issues, warnings, info } where each entry is { check, message }. Issues are blocking (solve will likely fail); warnings are non-fatal. Use this before solving to catch common configuration mistakes.

tools.name: list_constraints
tools.description: List all constraints in the network, including their active status and language.

tools.name: create_constraint
tools.description: A custom constraint, applied when the model solves. For one scenario only, create it with is_active false, then edit_constraint active true in that scenario. DSL (recommended, constraint_language='dsl'): `SUM(Generator.p WHERE carrier = "coal") <= 0.3 * DEMAND()`, `SUM(Generator.p_nom_opt WHERE carrier = "solar") >= 500`, `TOTAL(Generator.p WHERE carrier = "gas") <= 1000000` (MWh); SUM, TOTAL, COUNT, DEMAND(), EMISSIONS(), WHERE carrier/bus, FOR EACH PERIOD/BUS/DAY/WEEK/MONTH, >= <= ==. Python (constraint_language='python'): code on the network `n` (its optimisation model is `n.model`), with `pd`, `np`. The code is checked first; check_only: true only checks it. Or, instead of code, template {kind: build_rate|capacity_cap|land_limit|renewable_share|emissions_cap|reserve_margin, carriers, bus, mw_per_year, max_mw, area_km2, km2_per_mw, share, tonnes, margin}: written for you, and checked against fixed capacity.

name.description: Name of the constraint (e.g. 'Min Wind Generation', 'CO2 Cap')

constraint_code.description: The constraint code in DSL or Python

is_active.description: Whether the constraint is active (default true)

tools.name: edit_constraint
tools.description: Change a constraint by name: constraint_code replaces its code (checked first); active switches it on or off in scenario ("base" for the model itself); delete: true removes it, only with the user's word.

tools.name: assess_model
tools.description: The model as an analyst sees it: size, dimensions with values (carriers, scenarios, time config), which scenarios are solved, its problem type, and the metrics it can produce (available_metrics) or not (unsupported_metrics). For a question about what a model can answer; not needed before get_results, which reads results directly and names what it cannot answer.

tools.name: get_results
tools.description: Any solved result, or a model input (input_capacity, input_demand, availability: no run needed), as one table in one unit (columns, then rows; with 2+ dimensions carriers, components or buses become columns). Name a metric, split it with by, pick scenarios (["solved"] for every solved one; default the open one). year = investment period. E.g. {metric:"capacity", by:["year","carrier"], scenarios:["solved"]}; {metric:"price", by:["time"], time:{every:"month"}} (every:"duration" for a duration curve); one day: {metric:"generation", by:["time","carrier"], time:{from:"2040-07-07"}}. Metrics: capacity, storage_capacity, transmission_capacity, generation, demand, emissions, capital_cost, operating_cost, system_cost, unmet_load, price, state_of_charge, curtailment, capacity_factor, revenue, market_value, capture_rate, lcoe, input_capacity, input_demand, availability. IRP: npv (rate, base_year), new_build, retirements, clean_share_of_new_build (by year), share_of_load (carriers); each says its method.

metric.description: One metric name from the list.

by.description: Dimensions to split by. Empty = one total per scenario.

scenarios.description: Scenario names or ids, "base", or ["solved"] for every solved scenario. Default: the open scenario.

time.description: With by "time": every = step|hour|day|week|month|year|duration|histogram (default chosen by span); how = sum|mean|min|max. from / to ("2040-07-07", or "2040-07-07T16:00"; a date alone for to means to the end of it) or dates (["2040-07-07"]) narrow it to those days; from alone as a date means that one day. histogram: hours spent in each value bin (time is the bin); bins = a count (default 10) or edges; normalize:"peak" bins each series as % of its own peak; share:true gives % of hours; with by "year", one histogram per year.

bins.description: histogram: a bin count, or the bin edges.

top.description: Keep the N largest carriers/components/buses; the rest become "Other".

layout.description: wide (default): with 2+ dimensions, carriers (or components, buses) become columns. long: one row per value.

tools.name: diagnose_infeasibility
tools.description:
Diagnose why the model is (or was) infeasible. Runs structural checks against the live model state — bus capacity gaps, hourly supply/demand mismatch, disconnected components, time-axis misalignment, zero-availability renewables — and returns ranked findings with suggested fixes and view anchors.
ALWAYS call this immediately after any solve result with status='infeasible'. Also useful pre-solve to catch show-stoppers cheaply. Solver-agnostic.

scenario_id.description: Which scenario to read: a named scenario by its id (the uuid exactly as it was shown to you) or its name, or the string "base" for the Base Scenario (the as-built network — it has NO id of its own, so never pass a guessed id for it). Omit to use the current scenario. Omit to diagnose the current scenario.

tools.name: get_component_timeseries
tools.description: A summary of one timeseries (length, min/max/mean, p05/p50/p95, zeros, first and last values): demand (p_set), output (p), capacity factors (p_max_pu), prices, state of charge. full: true adds up to max_points raw values.

scenario_id.description: Optional scenario id (the uuid exactly as it was shown to you) or name, or "base" for the base network. If omitted, returns the timeseries for the currently-active scenario.

tools.name: set_series
tools.description: Fill a whole timeseries on the model's time axis without sending its values. One source: from_file {path, column, sheet} (a project file; by its time column, else one row per period), constant, per_year {"2030": v} (holds until the next year), or daily (24 hourly values). scale_to {"2030": total} then scales each year to sum to its total (value × hours, e.g. MWh for p_set); with no source it scales the current series. preview: true shows the result without writing.

scenario.description: Required: where the change goes. A what-if scenario by name or id (create_scenarios makes one), or "base" for the model itself, only when the user asked to change the model.

tools.name: fix_build
tools.description: Fix a solved scenario's build: makes scenario name as a copy of from, with every extendable component set to the capacity that solve chose and no longer extendable, so running it is dispatch only. It does not run it.

tools.name: write_chart
tools.description: Save a chart as code into the project's Analytics, creating or replacing by name; the app redraws it wherever it is shown, after every solve. set_dashboard puts it on a dashboard; gallery charts need no code. Name the chart by its data with `chart` (a get_results query and how to draw it), e.g. capacity by year, stacked by carrier: {query: {metric: "capacity", by: ["year", "carrier"]}, type: "bar", x: "year", color: "carrier"}. Write `source` only for what a query cannot show; call with neither for the code contract.

name.description: Chart name, unique in the project.

chart.description: A chart named by its data: query = get_results arguments; x and color = dimensions in query.by, or "scenario" to compare scenarios in one panel. x "time" with color "year" overlays the years on a time-of-year axis. histogram: hours at each level of the metric; color up to two dimensions.

bins.description: histogram: a bin count (default 10), or the bin edges.

normalize.description: histogram: bin each series as % of its own peak.

line.description: With x "time": a metric drawn as a line over it, e.g. "demand".

strips.description: x "time": up to 2 panels under it: a gallery time chart ("dispatch", {chart, off}) or metric.

source.description: The whole module: `export const reads` and the default chart function.

save_anyway.description: Save even though the check fails: only when it fails because the model has no results yet.

strips.description: With only name: set a saved chart's strips ([] clears).

tools.name: list_charts
tools.description: The open model's charts and dashboards, by name, with the charts failing to draw on screen. name reads one: a chart's source, or a dashboard's charts and the scenarios it draws.

tools.name: delete_chart
tools.description: Remove a chart (dashboards lose its card) or, with dashboard: true, a dashboard (its charts stay). Ask before removing one you did not make in this session.

tools.name: set_dashboard
tools.description: Create or replace a project dashboard: charts and notes on a grid. Charts draw `models` ({ chart, models } for one chart): one model by name with scenarios ("base", "open" = open in the app, or names; default "open"), side by side or overlaid. Without models: the open model for `scenarios` (none follows the open one); name solved ones, not asking. Charts come from write_chart / list_charts by name, or the gallery by id, each saved into the project first. Then show_address("[[dashboard:Name]]") shows it. This replaces only the dashboard named. With only name and size, it resizes that dashboard’s cards in place, keeping their order and its settings.

charts.description: Chart names, in order; laid out two to a row. A { note: markdown } in the list is a card of text instead: the points beside a chart, in the app’s type, wrapping to the card, with no title bar. Markdown takes **bold**, lists, links, [[component:Name]] mentions and > for a muted caption line.

gallery.description: Built-in charts to add after the named ones.

scenarios.description: Scenario names or ids, "base"/null for the base network. Omit to follow the app’s open scenario.

compare.description: How several scenarios are drawn (default side by side).

size.description: Every card’s size: smallest (four a row), small (three), medium (two, the default), large (full width).

tools.name: set_values
tools.description: Change input values in the scenario scenario_id names (a what-if keeps the base unchanged). Each change picks components (component, components, or component_type and/or carrier) and an attribute, then: a value to set; op multiply|add|clip_min|clip_max with amount to rescale a time series (year/month/hour filters); or op reset to drop the override. bus, built_from and built_to also pick. op decline: value × (1−rate)^(build_year − base_year), held at stop_year; op share_of: amount × the component's own `of` value; op retire with year (attribute lifetime): gone from that investment year on. Many changes, one call. from_file {path, sheet, component_column, columns: {attribute: column}} adds one change per row, each cited to the file. Values read from a project file by hand: give source {path, sheet, row} (on the call, or per change) and each is cited to it.

scenario_id.description: Required: where the change goes. A what-if scenario by name or id (create_scenarios makes one), or "base" for the model itself, only when the user asked to change the model.

replace_timeseries.description: true to replace a series with one value.

source.description: The project file the values came from.
The project file the values came from.

tools.name: create_scenarios
tools.description: Make what-if scenarios: scenarios, each with a name and optional overrides (component, attribute, value), or sweep, one scenario per value of an attribute across components. from copies another scenario's changes first. Returns their ids; base is "base". A name "set/member" groups scenarios into an ensemble.

tools.name: edit_scenario
tools.description: Rename a scenario or change its description; delete: true deletes it with its overrides and results (ask first unless the user asked).

tools.name: history
tools.description: What changed and who changed it. of "project" (default): files, documents and model edits, newest first (model or path narrows it). of "versions": the project's saved versions (each a point in time of the whole project). of "changes": what a version changed, counted per table.

tools.name: app_state
tools.description: Where you are: the model file this server works on (writable or not), and whether a Convexity app is running with the project, model and scenario it has open, and this server's version. With no model yet, this session starts working on the one the app shows. Cheap; call it first.

tools.name: solve_via_desktop_app
tools.description: Solve the open .db FILE through the running Convexity desktop app: queues one job per scenario in the app's Job Queue — free, on this computer, results written into the file in place, so the results tools read them once desktop_app_jobs reports it completed. A model that lives in the app (opened with open_in_app) is solved with run_model. Do not edit the model while its solve is running. Returns at once; solves take minutes.

scenario_ids.description: Scenario ids to solve (null = base case). Omit to solve the active scenario.

solver_name.description: Solver engine installed locally; 'highs' is always available, 'mosek' only with a local licence.

wait.description: Block until the jobs finish (progress is reported), then return their outcome. Default false: return as soon as they are queued.

timeout_seconds.description: With wait: give up waiting after this long (default 900).

max_parallel_jobs.description: How many of the queued scenarios may solve at once.

tools.name: desktop_app_jobs
tools.description: Jobs in the running Convexity desktop app's queue (solves, imports, exports), newest first, or one job by id.

tools.name: desktop_app_job_logs
tools.description: The tail of a desktop-app job's worker log (solver output) — use it to explain a failed local solve.

tools.name: account_status
tools.description: The signed-in Convexity account: which cloud features the organisation has enabled (cloud solve, solvers, data APIs, playbook signing, MCP access) and which Modelverse models it may open. Call it before promising a cloud feature, or to explain a refusal.

tools.name: get_open_model
tools.description: Report which model .db file this server is currently operating on, and whether it is writable or read-only (and why). Call this first when the user names a file, to check it matches.

tools.name: open_model
tools.description: Work on a Convexity model FILE: absolute path to a .db on disk. All subsequent tools operate on it, and edits are written in place — suggest the user works on a copy of any model they care about. A model that lives in the Convexity app is opened with open_in_app instead. Resets the active scenario to the base case. A file older than schema 4.0 is not opened in place: pass upgrade_copy: true to write a converted copy beside it and open that.

upgrade_copy.description: For a pre-4.0 file: write <name>-4.1.db beside it (the original is not touched) and open the copy.

tools.name: use_scenario
tools.description: Set the active scenario for all subsequent tool calls: a scenario name or id from list_scenarios, or "base" (or null) for the base case.

scenario.description: Scenario name or id, or "base" for the base case. Also accepted as scenario_id.

instructions:
Convexity MCP: builds, edits and analyses Convexity energy-system models, in a project of the running Convexity app or in a .db file.

1. Orient: app_state says where you are; with nothing open, you work on the model the app shows. open_in_app opens another app model by name, open_model a .db file by absolute path.
2. Know what the model is for (get_model_summary): horizon, historical or forward-looking, dispatch or expansion. Say plainly when a question is outside it, and what it can answer instead.
3. Numbers come from get_results (a metric by scenario, year, carrier, bus, time); a chart is its query. Never estimate.
4. Why: the reasons are in the project's Files (search_project_files, read_project_file), its sources (get_sources) and its history (history). Cite what you use.
5. What-ifs go in a scenario: create_scenarios (a sweep for a range), then set_values or add_components with that scenario (a constraint: create it inactive, activate it there); the Base Scenario stays as it is. Change the model itself only when it is empty or the user asks: add_components to "base", set_series for series, edit_components, edit_carriers. How it solves (e.g. representative days): run_settings. A what-if has no numbers until run: say a run is needed, never estimate. Run: run_model({wait: true}); runs lists the runs. A .db file uses solve_via_desktop_app({wait: true}).
6. Show, don't describe: show_address puts a [[component:…]], [[scenario:…]], [[dashboard:…]] or [[file:…]] on screen; show_in_app opens a page or a table; write_chart and set_dashboard build results pages. Draw a clear chart request, don't ask: with several solved scenarios draw them all and say which; with no dashboard, make one.
7. Stop once the task is done: report in a few lines. Deleting anything needs the user's word.

App models are shared and have no undo; a .db file gets a backup before the first edit. It runs no Python or SQL; never read .db files. A new kind of task (a review, a scenario study): read_skill its note; convexity://guide has more.
